reuse.why: Reuses budget writes, averaging, batching, and undo wrappers, but bypasses the new bulk selector in copyPreviousMonth and existing shared tag extraction in isFixedGroup.

duplication.why: Consolidates the average actions but retains a second implementation of bulk eligibility and introduces separate tag recognition logic.

placement.why: Budget selection and mutations stay in the budget action layer and registration stays in app.ts, although tag recognition belongs with the existing shared tag utilities.

scope.why: Changes are focused on the requested month-wide actions, their registration, supporting tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selector and average dispatcher improve ownership, but future eligibility changes still require coordinated updates to copyPreviousMonth and the selector.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth independently applies the eligibility policy centralized in getBulkEditableCategories, and isFixedGroup uses its own regex instead of shared/tags.ts extractTagsFromText.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses bulk eligibility as early returns while getBulkEditableCategories splits the same policy between SQL and filtering; isFixedGroup reshapes existing tag extraction into a dedicated regex.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkEditableCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and a conditional SQL hidden filter, while copyPreviousMonth bypasses that shared selector and maintains its own eligibility checks.
